# The verified state of the incoming branch is cached so the driver runs (one per
# conflicting path) do not repeat the work. An aborted merge leaves that file
# behind, so it is bound to the revision it was verified for - otherwise the next
# merge would inherit whatever the previous one was allowed to do.

sesam-repo admin base.txt good.txt ours.txt broken.txt

cp $TMPDIR/base.txt s
exec sesam add s --group admin
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'add s'

# A: a perfectly ordinary branch that verifies.
exec git checkout -b good
cp $TMPDIR/good.txt s
exec sesam seal
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'good: change s'

# B: same repo, changes the same secret, but also carries an object that no audit
# entry accounts for - so the branch as a whole does not verify.
exec git checkout -b broken master
cp $TMPDIR/broken.txt s
exec sesam seal
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'broken: change s'
cp .sesam/objects/s.sesam .sesam/objects/ghost.sesam
exec git add .sesam/objects/ghost.sesam
exec git commit --no-verify -m 'broken: unaccounted object'

exec git checkout master
cp $TMPDIR/ours.txt s
exec sesam seal
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'ours: change s'

# Merge A: it verifies, and its state is parked for the driver runs.
! exec git merge good
exec sh -c 'ls .sesam/tmp/theirs-vstate-*.json'
stdout 'theirs-vstate-'

# Abort. Nothing runs sesam, so the parked state survives.
exec git merge --abort
exec sh -c 'ls .sesam/tmp/theirs-vstate-*.json'

# Merging B must NOT ride on the state verified for A.
! exec git merge broken
stderr 'does not verify - refusing to merge it'

-- base.txt --
BASE
-- good.txt --
GOOD
-- ours.txt --
OURS
-- broken.txt --
BROKEN
